skill.name: azure-cloud-migrate
skill.description: Assess and guide migrations from AWS, Google Cloud, Heroku, App Engine, Kubernetes, and Spring workloads to Azure services.
skill.summary: Create assessment reports and migration guidance for moving cloud workloads to Azure.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives from Markdown links, code fences, Azure managed identity examples, and visible migration commands. Confirmed risks remain where the guides retrieve shared keys, export Kubernetes secrets, or pass decoded secret values through command-line arguments during migration.

remediation.issue: Decoded secrets are passed with az keyvault secret set --value in Kubernetes and Cloud Run migration examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace --value secret transfer with protected file input, stdin-safe tooling, or a documented manual step that avoids process arguments and shell history.

remediation.issue: Kubernetes exports include Secret resources in local YAML output.
remediation.suggestion: Exclude Secret objects from broad exports by default, or write redacted metadata only unless the user explicitly approves secret migration.

remediation.issue: Some deployment examples retrieve Log Analytics or storage account shared keys into shell variables.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer identity-based or keyless Azure Monitor and storage patterns, and clearly mark shared-key fallbacks as sensitive manual operations.

remediation.issue: Temporary files are used for secret import flows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep restrictive permissions and cleanup, but warn users not to run those steps in shared, recorded, or synchronized workspaces.

content.value_statement: Cloud migrations require careful service mapping, code changes, and deployment planning. This skill guides assessment and migration work for Azure Functions, App Service, and Container Apps.
actual_capabilities: Generates migration assessment reports before code changes.
Maps AWS Lambda triggers to Azure Functions triggers and bindings.
Maps Heroku, Elastic Beanstalk, and App Engine apps to Azure App Service.
Maps Kubernetes, Fargate, Cloud Run, and Spring workloads to Azure Container Apps.
Provides runtime-specific Azure Functions examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C#, Java, and PowerShell.
Prepares handoff context for Azure infrastructure, validation, and deployment steps.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated migration artifacts, not guaranteed production readiness.
It requires accurate source project files and cloud configuration from the user.
It cannot validate cloud costs, quotas, or live permissions without environment access.
Deployment commands can affect real cloud resources and must be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Assess Lambda migration readiness
use_cases.description: Inventory Lambda functions, triggers, dependencies, and IAM mappings before moving to Azure Functions.

use_cases.title: Plan web app migration
use_cases.description: Map Heroku, Elastic Beanstalk, or App Engine applications to Azure App Service with configuration and identity guidance.

use_cases.title: Move container workloads
use_cases.description: Evaluate Kubernetes, Fargate, Cloud Run, or Spring workloads for Azure Container Apps compatibility and deployment planning.

prompt_templates.title: Assess my source workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this project for Azure migration. Identify the source platform, required Azure target services, blockers, and the next files you need from me.

prompt_templates.title: Create a migration report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the required migration assessment report for this workload. Include service mapping, dependencies, security mapping, effort, risks, and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Convert service configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this source platform configuration to the closest Azure target configuration. Keep the original app unchanged and write all output to the Azure migration folder.

prompt_templates.title: Design a phased Azure migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased migration plan from assessment through deployment. Include identity, secrets, networking, observability, rollback, and validation steps for each phase.

output_examples.input: A repository contains three AWS Lambda functions with S3, SQS, and API Gateway triggers.
output: A migration assessment report lists each function, runtime, trigger, dependency, and Azure Functions equivalent.
The report recommends managed identity, binding-first code changes, and infrastructure handoff tasks.

output_examples.input: A Heroku app uses Postgres, Redis, config vars, a Procfile, and a worker process.
output: The migration plan maps the web process to Azure App Service and the worker to WebJobs or Container Apps.
Secrets are assigned to Key Vault references, and database access is moved toward managed identity where supported.

output_examples.input: A Kubernetes namespace contains deployments, services, ingress, secrets, and persistent volumes.
output: The assessment separates supported Container Apps resources from blockers such as StatefulSets or unsupported storage.
The plan describes image migration, service discovery updates, Key Vault use, and validation tests.

best_practices: Run the assessment phase and review the report before requesting code migration.
Review every generated cloud command before execution in a live subscription or project.
Use managed identity and Key Vault references instead of copying secrets into files or command arguments.
anti_patterns: Skipping the assessment report and moving directly to deployment commands.
Running generated migration commands against production without review and backups.
Storing decoded secrets, connection strings, or cloud keys in the workspace.

faq.question: Which Azure targets does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Functions, Azure App Service, and Azure Container Apps migration guidance.

faq.question: Does it modify my original source project?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to write migration output to a separate Azure folder.

faq.question: Can it deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: It includes deployment examples and handoff guidance, but users should approve and review commands first.

faq.question: Does it support Kubernetes migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It assesses Kubernetes workloads and maps supported patterns to Azure Container Apps.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It recommends managed identity and Key Vault, but some examples still require careful secret-handling review.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production migrations?
faq.answer: It is useful for planning and artifact generation, but production changes need human review, testing, and rollback planning.
